timeline.text: Take-Two files four DMCA notices on GitHub, all against GTA V ports. None names a GTA VI project.
The Xbox build's executable leaks, according to press reports; PC port projects start testing.
The original Leonida repo goes private and its creator steps away.
VIctory shows the first mission's title card; reproduced on a second PC.
Leonida CE presents its first (black) frames.
Leonida CE clears its audio stop; next stop is a double free at about 2 minutes.
five-star-recomp reaches the story intro's title card.
A Leonida CE run gets past its 2-minute crash and starts loading the world.
Leonida Continued: an integration PR reaches the first-run menus on Windows, the first Leonida build to show the game's UI.
Palmwave's repository was removed (404); it is no longer tracked. It had loaded the world with sound but no picture.

projects.status:
**Not playable yet, because of the framerate: about 1 frame per second in the
world.** Nothing else keeps the game from working: the title boots, runs its
menus at its own 30 fps, loads the world, plays the intro cutscene and
reaches the **prologue**, the mission after it, with the graphics fully
displayed. 

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about a minute) | works |
| The intro cutscene | plays at about 1 fps (0.9-1.0 s a frame, warm cache, quiet machine): textured and lit characters with whole hair, buildings, sky, depth of field, the title card, credits and interface. Missing: ray-traced shadows and indirect light, the local-light shadow mask. Seen in some shots: a pink band over nearer bodies, a stand-in head on a secondary character for a few frames |
| The prologue | reached; the graphics are fully displayed, at about 1 fps |

In the intro cutscene at 1 fps the opening credits land over other shots than
on a console: they follow the frame count, the shots follow the clock.

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT (12 GB).

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU hung it in earlier builds,
> and Windows then reset the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). The latest runs, several minutes each in the world, did not, but
> it is not ruled out; a run can also end on a GPU fault (`crashes.log`). A
> diagnostics build with `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` renders on the software
> adapter instead (too slow to reach the world in minutes).

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | The scene is drawn and presented: mesh pipelines, indirect execution, views the shaders pick from the heap themselves, title memory read by address, depth written from compute, lists that wait for values other queues write, textures made when a shader first reads them, pipelines pre-built or made by worker threads and kept on disk, depth bounds on supporting adapters (synthetic tests) | The title's ray-tracing structures are never built (no ray-traced shadows or indirect light in the intro cutscene); about 1 s a frame; draws of untranslated shaders are dropped; real queries, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL, ahead of time (`translate --cache`) or at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: all but under 300 of 24,387 programs | Merged geometry stages (195 programs) and under 100 others; fused multiply-adds follow the host GPU; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Menus, loading and the world run with the PC upscaler (`VICTORY_FIDELITYFX_DIR`, about 1 s a frame) | The title's own upscaler DLLs: six of their passes are untranslated, so their picture is wrong |

projects.notes:
## 2026-11-24 (later): after console footprints (9bd2a8d)

- The 2.2 GB GPU pool (title allocator 2, object at 0x1471c2808: base +0x20, size +0x30 = 0x89700000, used
  +0x58) no longer fills: allocation answers are console footprints now. The title runs to about 124 s and
  binds its UI pipelines (VertexCxformEAlpha, BatchVertexCxformEAlpha); frames are still all zero.
- Next stop at about 124 s: soft asserts in the title's free (game+0x1887b0; +0x187fb, +0x1881f, +0x1884a check
  the block header at -0x10/-0xc/-0x2), then a null read at +0x538d0e6 under a recursive teardown
  (+0x183aaf / +0x18435f). A block freed there is not from that heap, or its header was overwritten.
- The bad free (gdb, break at game+0x1400187fb with the other soft asserts patched to nop): the block's
  allocated bit (header word at -0x2, bit 10) is clear, so it was already freed (double free) or its header was
  overwritten; its payload is float data (1.0f). It is freed by a container's teardown (game+0x455aeb0: count at
  +0x32, entries at +0x38, each freed through the allocator at 0x14abcc310, vtable +0x60), under +0x515ad70.
  Teardown at this point is an error path: something earlier failed. The first anomaly in the run is a write
  past a stream buffer's capacity at about 98 s (soft assert +0x4dcbc9d, game+0x4dcbc55: remaining < size;
  the write is skipped and returns false). Next: what fills that buffer, and why it is too small here.
- The overflowing buffer (game+0x4dcbc55, about 100 s) is a shared command stream, not a DSP queue: records
  tagged 0x...04002821 carry float parameters (0.55, 0.2, 1000, 2000). Writers flush a local buffer into it
  (game+0x4e52a40: lock at owner+8, append via +0x4dcbc40) from +0x5ab13e8 through +0x4e529a0. The stream comes
  from the table at *0x149ae9950 (+0x4dcbc10): per slot an object with several 0x28-byte streams and a current
  index at +0xc8, so a consumer is meant to switch streams each frame and drain the old one (the switch is in the
  large function around +0x4dc3df2/+0x4dc3e11). No thread was in that code in the stack dumps, and the stream fills
  in about 100 s. A null ALSA device (ALSA_CONFIG_PATH with pcm.!default type null, run setting only) removed the
  ALSA open errors but did not change this. Next: who calls the switch, and what it waits on.
- gdb from 20 s to 280 s: the stream append (+0x4dcbc72) runs on several threads (gdb threads 27, 96), about
  1,000 times in that window; neither write of the stream index (+0x4dc3e11, +0x4dc2e23) ever runs. Either the
  consumer is elsewhere or its thread never runs. AcpHal now acknowledges commands (97ca179), but the title only
  registers for messages (command 2) before this stop, so the coprocessor is not what the consumer waits on.
  gdb note: a breakpoint must be on an instruction boundary (check game.asm), or the run breaks silently.
- The stream consumer, found: game+0x43a6b40 walks every stream-table entry (count at 0x149ae9958) and is called
  only from the manage

projects.status:
GTA VI does not run yet. Its main executable is now available: under the loader it starts, runs through its memory
set-up, archive opening and graphics device set-up, presents frames to its own window, shows its logo, intro art and
first-run screens, loads story mode and plays the opening cutscene's art, credit cards, dialogue and sound at 30 frames
a second. The world's lit image now reaches the screen (the night sky, clouds and the city on the horizon), but its
surfaces are still black (their material textures are being fixed), and world frames take about a second each.
Details and numbers are in the
[wiki](https://github.com/ThatRecompDev/five-star-recomp/wiki/Status).

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Shader translation | Every shader stage the game uses is translated (vertex, pixel, compute, mesh, geometry, ray intersection), and all 25,908 programs compile. Branches become structured `if`/`else` and loops, 39% smaller than the older dispatch loop and checked to give the same results on real programs. Instruction behaviour is checked on D3D12 WARP. Shaders are translated when the game first uses them and compiled by a DXIL backend of our own, 5 to 20 times faster than dxc, in a separate compile process; dxc remains the fallback. |
| Archives | Contents can be extracted without the encrypted file table (no names yet). Metadata files parse completely. |
| Textures | Every texture decodes exactly with the BCPack tables, which you supply yourself (`fivestar setup --bcpack-tables`); without them 99.44% are readable and BC7, BC6H and BC3 (about 2,000 textures) are not. |
| Models | Drawable geometry (meshlets, packed vertices) decodes and exports as OBJ ([docs/models.md](docs/models.md)). |
| Loader | The game executable and its support libraries load with all imports resolved; the game boots through its start-up, answers its first-run screens through a scripted gamepad ([docs/first-run.input](docs/first-run.input)) and starts loading story mode. The console runtime, audio decoding and system libraries are implemented for offline use. |
| Graphics API | The game's D3D12.X device runs on desktop D3D12: its pipelines build from the translated shaders (with a disk cache), its descriptors and barriers are translated, and it presents its logo, intro video and menus with complete UI text. Shaders that read memory through console GPU addresses reach the game's memory through an address map. The GPU hang after the story load (shader loops that never ended) is bounded; open: the story load itself, which stops on corrupted game memory ([docs/d3d12x-shim.md](docs/d3d12x-shim.md)). |

The [wiki](../../wiki) has the details, research notes and the current progress report.

Forward the window and message functions to user32

projects.status:
Early development. **Nothing is playable yet.**

| Milestone | State |
|---|---|
| M0: PE readers, `.pdata`-seeded function discovery, import table | In progress: readers, discovery, and jump-table resolution are done and tested against the side DLLs of build 1.0.2.1 |
| M1: the native loader runs the game's code; imports, exceptions, TLS, and heaps work | In progress: the loader, hook engine, import policy, and pre-flight scan are done and tested on original fixtures, and the game's side DLLs initialize under it |
| M2: threads, memory, and I/O stable through boot | Started: the install is mounted read-only and the path functions run on it; the Game Runtime's task queues and async calls are implemented and tested |
| M3: first frame, then the title screen | Not started |
| M4: in-game and controllable | Not started |
| M5: enhancements, settings UI, Linux under Proton verified | Not started |
